definition: Natural language understanding (NLU) or natural language interpretation (NLI) is a subset of natural language processing in artificial intelligence that deals with machine reading comprehension.
details: NLU has been considered an AI-hard problem. There is considerable commercial interest in the field because of its application to automated reasoning, machine translation, question answering, news-gathering, text categorization, voice-activation, archiving, and large-scale content analysis.

explainer.lead: NLU is the part of NLP that gets a machine to actually read and comprehend text, not just process its surface. It matters because most commercial value in language AI — answering questions, reasoning over text, categorising documents — depends on it.

tiers.eli5: It's teaching a computer to understand what a sentence means, the way a person does when reading a book, rather than just spotting the words.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use NLU to turn raw text into structured meaning for downstream tasks like question answering and classification. A common pitfall is that ambiguous or messy real-world input breaks comprehension models that looked fine on clean benchmarks.
tiers.paperLevel: NLU, also called natural language interpretation, is the subset of natural language processing concerned with machine reading comprehension. It is widely regarded as an AI-hard problem, with no general solution.

explainer.example: A support system reads a customer email, extracts that the complaint is about a delayed refund, and routes it to the billing queue.
